[Boards](/boards) / All-in-one boards

7" 800x480 RGB panel with GT911 touch, a TF card slot, RS485, CAN and a sensor input. Same wiring as the 4.3" board, its own timings.

![The Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 board](/img/boards/waveshare-s3-7.webp)

Photograph: [Waveshare](https://www.waveshare.com/media/catalog/product/e/s/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-7-1.jpg) · vendor product photo, no licence stated

## Building for it

A project is made for one toolchain, picked when you start it. All three can drive this board:

Toolchain

**Arduino (C++)**

Every board, every widget and every peripheral here. The most control, and the most to set up. [Start a project](https://app.lcdwizard.com/app?board=waveshare-s3-7&target=arduino)

**MicroPython**

Change a screen by editing a file on the board. No compiler once it is flashed. [Start a project](https://app.lcdwizard.com/app?board=waveshare-s3-7&target=micropython)

**ESPHome**

No compiler to install, and the panel can join Home Assistant as real entities. [Start a project](https://app.lcdwizard.com/app?board=waveshare-s3-7&target=esphome)

**ESP-IDF (C)**

Espressif's own framework: esp\_lcd, the component registry and idf.py, with nothing of Arduino in it. [Start a project](https://app.lcdwizard.com/app?board=waveshare-s3-7&target=espidf)

## At a glance

Part

Detail

Maker

Waveshare

MCU

ESP32-S3  
Xtensa LX7 dual-core @ 240 MHz, 512 KB SRAM (+ 2-16 MB PSRAM on most modules)

Display

Generic RGB565 panel, 800 x 480 px, RGB565 parallel (DPI), 16-bit colour

Touch

Goodix GT911 (capacitive, I2C)

Backlight

CH422G pin 2, on and off

Memory

16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM (N16R8)

Graphics library

GFX Library for Arduino

## Display pins

Generic RGB565 panel on RGB565 parallel (DPI): RGB colour order, inversion off.

Signal

Pin

DE

GPIO 5

VSYNC

GPIO 3

HSYNC

GPIO 46

PCLK

GPIO 7

R0 - R4

GPIO 1, 2, 42, 41, 40

G0 - G5

GPIO 39, 0, 45, 48, 47, 21

B0 - B4

GPIO 14, 38, 18, 17, 10

RESET

CH422G pin 3

Backlight

CH422G pin 2

## Touch pins

GT911: I2C address 0x5D, 400 kHz.

Signal

Pin

SDA

GPIO 8

SCL

GPIO 9

INT / IRQ

GPIO 4

RESET

CH422G pin 1

## Also on the board

*   **I2C0 (touch, CH422G, header)** - SDA GPIO 8, SCL GPIO 9
*   **SPI (TF card)** - SCK GPIO 12, MOSI GPIO 11, MISO GPIO 13
*   **CH422G** I/O expander at 0x24, driving the lines marked above
*   **SDCard** - SD card, on SPI (TF card), CS CH422G pin 4  
    The TF card slot. Its CS is EXIO4 of the CH422G rather than a GPIO, so the card is selected once and stays selected, and has this SPI bus to itself.
*   **RS485** - RS485 / Modbus RTU, TX GPIO 16, RX GPIO 15  
    The A and B terminals. The transceiver turns itself round, so there is no direction pin - and the pins are the other way about from Waveshare's table, which names them from the transceiver's side.
*   **CanBus** - CAN bus / OBD-II, TX GPIO 20, RX GPIO 19, EN CH422G pin 5 (arrives switched off in a new design)  
    The CAN H and L terminals. It arrives switched off because GPIO 19 and 20 are also the USB port: switching this on raises EXIO5, which hands them to the CAN transceiver and takes the USB port away until the board is next powered up with it off. The UART port still flashes and logs.
*   CH422G pin 6 is set high at boot - Panel enable (EXIO6)
*   **Sensor AD** - analog input on GPIO 6

The preset adds these to the Hardware tab with the board, so a sensor can go straight onto the connector.

**Guide:** [Waveshare 4.3 and 7 inch boards: card slot, RS485, CAN and sensor input](/docs/waveshare-4-3-and-7) - each of these parts step by step, with what to wire, what to press and what to check when it does not answer.

**Check your revision.** Touch reset (EXIO1), backlight enable (EXIO2, DISP on the schematic), panel reset (EXIO3), the TF card's CS (EXIO4), the USB / CAN switch (EXIO5) and the panel's supply enable (EXIO6, LCD\_VDD\_EN) sit on a CH422G expander on the I2C bus at GPIO 8/9; the generated code brings the expander up first and drives them. ESPHome drives EXIO2 and EXIO6 together as enable pins, so if the panel is dark with the backlight apparently on, look at those two for your revision. The TF card is on SPI (MOSI 11, SCK 12, MISO 13) and must be the only thing on it: its CS cannot be toggled through the expander, so the card is selected once and stays selected. RS485 is an SP3485 that turns itself round - the chip sends on GPIO 16 and receives on GPIO 15, which is the other way about from Waveshare's pin table (it names the two from the transceiver's side). GPIO 19 and 20 are the USB port until EXIO5 is raised, which hands them to the CAN transceiver (TX 20, RX 19): the CAN bus arrives switched off, and switching it on takes the USB port away - the expander keeps its lines through a reset, so flash through the UART port, or power the board off and on. The Sensor AD terminal is GPIO 6, 0 to about 3.1 V. The serial log is the UART port (GPIO 43/44). Read off the schematic; nobody here has had this board in their hands.

## Designing for it in LCD Wizard

*   Choose **Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7** on the Hardware tab (or use the button above) and every pin on this page is filled in. The export writes the sketch, `lcd_pins.h`, the GFX Library for Arduino configuration, `lv_conf.h` and `platformio.ini` - a project that builds for this board as it comes.
*   The GT911 is capacitive and needs no calibration. The firmware resets it and checks it answers on every boot.
*   The backlight switches on and off; it is not dimmable from the firmware.
*   An RGB panel keeps its frame buffer in PSRAM, which this board has.
*   Screens are designed for 800 x 480 px in either orientation, with LVGL 9 or LVGL 8.

## The parts

**Generic RGB565 panel.** Raw RGB glass with no controller IC. All timing comes from the MCU.

**GT911.** The address is selected by the INT pin level during reset, so wire INT and RST if you can.

**ESP32-S3.** The only common Arduino target with a hardware RGB565 LCD peripheral. PSRAM is effectively required for RGB panels.

**GFX Library for Arduino.** Moshi Liu's library. Best QSPI/AMOLED and RGB coverage. Configured in code.

## The pinout on one page

Every pin above, laid out to print and keep beside the bench. Generated from this preset, so it says exactly what the designer writes into `lcd_pins.h`.

[Download the pinout (PNG)](/boards/waveshare-s3-7/pinout.png)[Open it as SVG](/boards/waveshare-s3-7/pinout.svg)

The same pins as data - `board.json` and `pins.csv` - are in the [open pinout dataset on GitHub](https://github.com/lildev1979/esp32-display-pinouts/tree/main/boards/waveshare-s3-7), free to reuse under CC BY 4.0.

## From the people who made it

The board’s own documentation. Pinouts on vendor pages do sometimes disagree with the hardware in front of you - where this page and that one differ, trust your board and tell us.

*   [The vendor’s product page](https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-7.htm?&aff_id=182657)
*   [Vendor documentation](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7)
*   [Schematic (PDF)](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7-Sch.pdf)
*   [ST7262 RGB panel controller datasheet](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/common/ST7262.pdf)
*   [CH422G I/O expander datasheet](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/common/CH422DS1_EN.pdf)

## Designs for this board

Nobody has published a design for this board yet. Publish yours from the designer and it appears here and in the [gallery](/gallery).

![](/img/boards/waveshare-s3-43-thumb.webp)**[Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4.3](/boards/waveshare-s3-43)**4.3" 800x480 RGB panel with GT911 touch, a TF card slot, RS485, CAN and a sensor input. An I/O expander handles the reset lines.ESP32-S3 · Generic RGB565 panel 800 x 480 · GT911 touch[Purchase this board](https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-4.3.htm?&aff_id=182657)

![](/img/boards/waveshare-s3-touch-lcd-28b-thumb.webp)**[Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2.8B](/boards/waveshare-s3-touch-lcd-28b)**2.8" 480x640 IPS panel (ST7701, RGB) with GT911 touch, a TF card slot, QMI8658 IMU, PCF85063 RTC and battery sense. A TCA9554 expander handles the panel's reset and chip select and the touch reset.ESP32-S3 · ST7701 / ST7701S 480 x 640 · GT911 touch[Purchase this board](https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-2.8b.htm?&aff_id=182657)

![](/img/boards/waveshare-s3-35b-thumb.webp)**[Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5B](/boards/waveshare-s3-35b)**3.5" 320x480 AXS15231B over QSPI with touch in the same chip, an ES8311 codec with a microphone and speaker output, IMU, RTC, battery charging, a TF card and a camera connector.ESP32-S3 · AXS15231B 320 x 480 · AXS15231B (touch half) touch[Purchase this board](https://www.waveshare.com/esp32-s3-touch-lcd-3.5b.htm?&aff_id=182657)

## Next

*   [Quick start](/docs/quick-start) - from an empty screen to firmware on the board
*   [Boards and displays](/docs/boards) - presets, controllers, pins and touch in the designer
*   [Flashing and configuration](/docs/flashing) - PlatformIO, the Arduino IDE and first-boot checks
*   [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) - a white screen, mirrored image or touch that misses

Now I have everything I need, including the Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel constructor semantics:

- `hsync_polarity=0` → `hsync_idle_low=1` (idle low, sync pulse active HIGH); `hsync_polarity=1` → idle high, sync active LOW.
- Waveshare demos don't set polarity flags → esp_lcd defaults (hsync_idle_low=0, vsync_idle_low=0) → idle high → sync active low. So in Arduino_GFX terms: hsync_polarity=1, vsync_polarity=1 to reproduce Waveshare behavior. Note: many community configs for ST7262 panels use polarity 0 and still work, but strictly Waveshare demo = esp_lcd defaults = idle high. LCD Wizard page doesn't list polarities explicitly. I'll give the demo-derived settings (polarity 1/1 matching esp_lcd defaults, pclk_active_neg=1) and note that ST7262 panels are commonly tolerant.

Note: in Arduino_GFX, hsync_polarity==0 → hsync_idle_low=1 (active-high pulse); ==1 → idle high. Waveshare demos idle high → polarity=1. But many ST7262 community configs (e.g. Guition/ESP32-8048S070) use polarity 0 and work; panel is polarity-tolerant. Also note bounce buffer: Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel by default... (bounce_buffer_size_px default 0 → direct); fb_in_psram=true hardcoded; single FB. Frame buffer 800×480×2=768KB fits in 8MB.

Also for backlight: cannot use Arduino_RGB_Display(bl_pin,...) because BL is on CH422G EXIO2 (not a GPIO). Use ESP32_IO_Expander: expander->digitalWrite(2, HIGH). Also must drive EXIO6 HIGH (panel VDD enable) and pulse EXIO3 (LCD reset). Per docs page: "IO_DISP, RST_IO, and BL_IO ... three pins are actually pulled high by the hardware" — wait, the docs code-review says these three expander lines are pulled high by hardware?? "These three pins are actually pulled high by the hardware." Interesting — meaning at boot the CH422G outputs default to input/high-impedance and pull-ups enable backlight/LCD_VDD, so even without driving the expander the screen works; but the 03 demo drives them high actively. LCD Wizard says ESPHome drives EXIO2 and EXIO6 together. Either way: recommend driving EXIO6 high, EXIO2 high, EXIO3 pulse low→high. Actually careful: if hardware pulls them high, the screen may just work. But to be safe port should set them.

CH422G quirk: expander lines hold their state through ESP32 reset (CH422G is separately powered) — noted by LCD Wizard for USB_SEL/CAN.

GT911 touch via I2C: use Wire(8,9), address 0x5D, RST=EXIO1 (CH422G pin 1), INT=GPIO4 (active-low falling). Reset sequence per board conf: INT low → TP_RST low 100ms → high 200ms → INT to input. Result address 0x5D.

I2C bus shared: CH422G + GT911 + external I2C header all on Wire (SDA=8, SCL=9)@400kHz. Avoid addresses 0x20-0x27, 0x30-0x3F, 0x5D.

USB: two ports; flash via either: "UART" port (CH343P → UART0 GPIO43/44 with auto-reset circuit) or native "USB" port (GPIO19/20, needs USB CDC / DFU boot). USB_SEL (EXIO5) LOW = native USB; HIGH = CAN (survives reset!). For the device firmware (ESP32-S3 device in agent-buddy: USB serial for the daemon), use native USB on GPIO19/20 with EXIO5 left low.

Also: Flash/PSRAM: N16R8 = 16MB flash (QIO @ 120MHz per wiki IDF config) + 8MB octal PSRAM (OPI, 120MHz: CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT, SPIRAM_SPEED_120M). In Arduino IDE: PSRAM "OPI PSRAM", Flash Mode "QIO 120MHz".

Schematic U8 marking says "ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R8" in the extracted text while wiki header says N16R8 — note as a minor doc inconsistency; current boards ship N16R8 per product page/wiki features ("16MB Flash and 8MB PSRAM"). LCD Wizard also says 16MB N16R8. Hmm, actually the wiki features list says "Built-in 512KB SRAM and 384KB ROM, with onboard 16MB Flash and 8MB PSRAM" while the wiki Specifications table says "Flash 8MB, PSRAM 8MB" — contradiction within wiki. I'll note it.

Audio: none. IMU: none. RTC: none (RTCN/RTCP nets are part of RS485 auto-direction circuit or boot strapping resistors, not an RTC).

Battery: PH2.0 3.7V lithium, CS8501 charger+5V boost, charge current 580mA (R45... well the wiki says replace R45; schematic PROG table 1.2K→580mA etc.), CHG/DONE LEDs, ≤2000mAh recommended.

"Sensor AD" terminal: GPIO6 (ADC2_CH2? the demo calls it PIN_ADC2_CH2=6 — GPIO6 is ADC1_CH5 actually, whatever, demo names it ADC2_CH2), 12-bit demo; header 3V3/AD/GND; 200K/100K divider + protection (TP1/R27 100R → so input range up to ~9.3V scales? or 0-3.1V per LCD Wizard). I'll just report GPIO6 with demo using analogRead 12-bit.

UART selection: SW1 (or the mux U13 selected how?) routes CH343P to ESP UART0 (GPIO43/44) or to external UART header H3 (EX_TXD/EX_RXD). Wiki: "6 and 7 are the same UART, selected by switch 15" — switch 15 = "UART selection jumper UART1 or UART2"... the wiki onboard list: "15. UART selection jumper UART1 or UART2". Hmm — that suggests switch selects whether the UART Type-C (CH343P) connects to... "UART1 or UART2"?? Odd phrasing; more likely "USB UART ↔ external UART header". Schematic: SW1 is a 6-pin slide switch selecting CH_RXD/CH_TXD → ESP_RXD/ESP_TXD vs EX_RXD/EX_TXD. Actually U13 FSUSB42UMX SEL comes from "UART_SEL" net "PIR501?" + SW1. The wiki says jumper 15 selects "UART1 or UART2" — I'll describe it factually: a slide switch routes the CH343P either to the ESP32-S3 UART0 (GPIO43/44, for flashing/logging) or to the external UART PH2.0 header.

Hmm wait, re-reading wiki: "7. UART terminal — 6 and 7 are the same UART, selected by switch 15" and "15. UART selection jumper — UART1 or UART2". The schematic shows EX_RXD/EX_TXD nets going where? "PAU1306/7 NLEX0RXD/NLEX0TXD PIH303/4" → H3 header (UART terminal J? "1 2 3 4 H3"). So switch chooses: CH343P ↔ ESP32_UART0 (GPIO43/44) OR external header ↔ ESP32_UART0. i.e., the ESP UART0 is what gets muxed between the USB-UART bridge and the external UART header. Wiki's "6 and 7 are the same UART, selected by switch 15" matches this: port 6 (USB-UART Type-C) and port 7 (UART terminal) are the same UART0, selected by switch. OK good.

CAN transceiver: TJA1051T/3 (5V, VIO 3.3V). S pin: "S 8" standby control — net "PIU708" → "NLSGND"? probably tied to GND = normal mode. Fine, mention normal mode.

Termination: J5 = CAN 120R selection; J4 = RS485 120R selection (R70/R75 120R, default connected per wiki: "jumpers connect 120 ohm resistor by default").

Now — one thing I haven't verified: CH422G EXIO0/EXIO7 usage. Wiki tables list EXIO1,2,4,5; EXIO3 (LCD_RST) and EXIO6 (LCD_VDD_EN) from demos/schematic. EXIO0 and EXIO7: OC0-OC3 pins — unused? LCD Wizard lists pin6 as panel enable. No evidence of EXIO0/EXIO7 use. Fine, say all expander lines consumed: EXIO1 TP_RST, EXIO2 DISP/BL_EN, EXIO3 LCD_RST, EXIO4 SD_CS, EXIO5 USB_SEL/CAN_SEL, EXIO6 LCD_VDD_EN; EXIO0/EXIO7 (and OC0–OC3 outputs) not used apparently.

Good. Time to write the research brief to /tmp/lcd7-research.md and also update the progress file. Then produce the final response with acceptance report.

Note the task mentions "Update progress at: .pi-subagents/artifacts/progress/.../progress.md" — I should write a progress note there. There's no instruction against writing; write tool is available. I'll write a brief progress update (completion) to that path.

# Research: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 — hardware pin-level brief for an Arduino_GFX firmware port

## Summary

The ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 is an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB QIO flash + 8 MB **octal** PSRAM) board driving a raw 800×480 RGB565 (ST7262-class, controller-less) panel over 20 GPIOs, with a GT911 touch, a **CH422G I2C IO-expander** handling backlight/panel-reset/panel-power/SD-CS/USB-CAN-mux, plus RS485, CAN, TF slot, two USB-C ports (native USB-OTG **and** a CH343P USB-UART bridge), and a 3.7 V battery charger. Waveshare's official demos do **not** use Arduino_GFX — they use ESP-IDF's esp_lcd RGB panel (either directly via ESP-IDF or via the ESP32_Display_Panel `BusRGB` + `LCD_ST7262` wrapper in Arduino). All timings/pins below map 1:1 onto `Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel` + `Arduino_RGB_Display`.

## Findings

### 1. RGB LCD panel

Panel is a 50-pin RGB glass with an **ST7262** driver (works "raw" — no SPI init commands, no D/C). 16-bit RGB565 bus on the upper bits of an RGB888 interface (B3–B7, G2–G7, R3–R7). Source: Waveshare wiki pinout table + schematic J1 connector + demo code.

**Sync/clock pins** ([wiki](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7), [demo header](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/blob/main/examples/Arduino/examples/08_DrawColorBar/waveshare_lcd_port.h)):

| Signal | GPIO |
|---|---|
| DE | 5 |
| VSYNC | 3 |
| HSYNC | 46 |
| PCLK | 7 |
| DISP / backlight | CH422G EXIO2 (not a GPIO) |
| LCD_RST | CH422G EXIO3 (not a GPIO) |

**16 data pins** — shown both as panel color bits and in `Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel` R0..R4/G0..G5/B0..B4 order, and in esp_lcd D0..D15 order (all three sources agree: [wiki](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7), [arduino-esp32 variant pins_arduino.h](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/3.3.10/variants/waveshare_esp32_s3_touch_lcd_7/pins_arduino.h), [ESP32_Display_Panel board config](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/blob/main/examples/Arduino/libraries/ESP32_Display_Panel/src/board/supported/waveshare/BOARD_WAVESHARE_ESP32_S3_TOUCH_LCD_7.h)):

| Panel bit | GPIO | Arduino_GFX arg | esp_lcd D# |
|---|---|---|---|
| B3 | 14 | b0 | 0 |
| B4 | 38 | b1 | 1 |
| B5 | 18 | b2 | 2 |
| B6 | 17 | b3 | 3 |
| B7 | 10 | b4 | 4 |
| G2 | 39 | g0 | 5 |
| G3 | 0 | g1 | 6 |
| G4 | 45 | g2 | 7 |
| G5 | 48 | g3 | 8 |
| G6 | 47 | g4 | 9 |
| G7 | 21 | g5 | 10 |
| R3 | 1 | r0 | 11 |
| R4 | 2 | r1 | 12 |
| R5 | 42 | r2 | 13 |
| R6 | 41 | r3 | 14 |
| R7 | 40 | r4 | 15 |

**Timing used in demos** (08_DrawColorBar + board config + wiki code review):
- PCLK = **16 MHz**; Bounce buffer = width×10 px (8000) to avoid screen drift; single frame buffer in PSRAM.
- HPW=4, HBP=8, HFP=8, VPW=4, VBP=8, VFP=8 (same values in both the Arduino demo and the ESP-IDF/LVGL board config).
- Polarities: demos leave esp_lcd defaults, i.e. `hsync_idle_low=0, vsync_idle_low=0, de_idle_high=0` (syncs idle **high** / pulses active low). Verified in `esp_panel_bus_rgb.cpp` `convertPartialToFull()`.
- PCLK edge: the LVGL/board-config path sets `PCLK_ACTIVE_NEG=1` (panel samples on falling edge). The positional-ctor path in 08_DrawColorBar leaves it 0 — the ST7262 tolerates both at this clock; use **1** to match Waveshare's board config.
- ESP-IDF LVGL benchmark note in the wiki mentions PCLK 21 MHz ≈ 51 Hz refresh (26 fps LVGL benchmark single-core). At 16 MHz refresh ≈ 39 Hz (16e6 / (820×500)).
- Resulting ~820 px/line, ~500 lines/frame.

**Arduino_GFX class mapping** — the demos are NOT Arduino_GFX; the matching classes are `Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel` + `Arduino_RGB_Display` (confirmed working by [LCD Wizard's board preset](https://lcdwizard.com/boards/waveshare-s3-7), which uses GFX Library for Arduino). Verified against Arduino_GFX source (`hsync_polarity==1 → hsync_idle_low=0`):

```cpp
Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel *rgbpanel = new Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel(
    5 /*DE*/, 3 /*VSYNC*/, 46 /*HSYNC*/, 7 /*PCLK*/,
    /*r0..r4*/ 1, 2, 42, 41, 40,
    /*g0..g5*/ 39, 0, 45, 48, 47, 21,
    /*b0..b4*/ 14, 38, 18, 17, 10,
    /*hsync_polarity*/1, /*hfp*/8, /*hpw*/4, /*hbp*/8,
    /*vsync_polarity*/1, /*vfp*/8, /*vpw*/4, /*vbp*/8,
    /*pclk_active_neg*/1, /*prefer_speed*/16000000L);
Arduino_RGB_Display *gfx = new Arduino_RGB_Display(800, 480, rgbpanel);
```

**Backlight: NOT a GPIO, NOT PWM.** It is CH422G **EXIO2** (net `DISP` → BL_EN of an **AP3032** boost LED driver on the LCD FPC VLED± rails), on/off only, active high. Source: wiki pinout table + [ESP32_Display_Panel board config](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7) (`BACKLIGHT_TYPE = SWITCH_EXPANDER, IO=2, ON_LEVEL=1`) + schematic (U3 AP3032). There is no PWM-capable route to the backlight without rewiring. Also note the panel supply (AVDD/VGH/VGL ~9.85 V via AP3012 + charge pumps) is gated by CH422G **EXIO6** (`LCD_VDD_EN`) — drive it high too. (wiki docs mention these three expander lines are hardware-pulled so the screen may light without driving them; the demos still drive them explicitly.)

### 2. Touch controller

**Goodix GT911** (capacitive, 5-point). Source: [ESP32_Display_Panel board config](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7) (`TOUCH_CONTROLLER GT911`), [LCD Wizard](https://lcdwizard.com/boards/waveshare-s3-7), wiki I2C scan table.

- I2C: **SDA=GPIO8, SCL=GPIO9**, 400 kHz (shared bus with CH422G and the external I2C header).
- Address: **0x5D** (default; 0x14 if INT is high at reset). The board-config reset sequence drives INT low during reset to select 0x5D; wiki scan confirms 0x5d occupied.
- **INT = GPIO4** (direct SoC pin, active low/falling). **RST = CH422G EXIO1** (`TP_RST`, via expander). Reset sequence from board config: INT output low 10 ms → EXIO1 low 100 ms → EXIO1 high → 200 ms → INT back to input.

### 3. IO expander — yes, CH422G

CH422G (16-pin, I2C) on the GPIO8/9 bus. Nominal "address" 0x24 in ESP32_IO_Expander which **ignores it** — CH422G uses fixed command addresses, so the nominal value differs by library (0x24 in `esp_io_expander_ch422g.h`, 0x20 in the ESP32_Display_Panel board conf); the wiki scan table shows rows 0x20–0x27 and 0x30–0x3F occupied. Demos construct `esp_expander::CH422G(scl=9, sda=8, ESP_IO_EXPANDER_I2C_CH422G_ADDRESS)` and call `enableAllIO_Output()`. Assignment (source: wiki pinout tables + `waveshare_lcd_port.h` / `waveshare_sd_card.h` + schematic net names + LCD Wizard):

| CH422G pin | Net | Function |
|---|---|---|
| EXIO1 | TP_RST / CTP_RST | GT911 reset |
| EXIO2 | DISP | Backlight enable (active high) |
| EXIO3 | LCD_RST | Panel reset (pulse low ≥10 ms) |
| EXIO4 | SD_CS | TF card chip-select, active low (demos just hold it low — card permanently selected, SPI bus exclusive to it) |
| EXIO5 | USB_SEL / CAN_SEL | GPIO19/20 routing mux (FSUSB42UMX): **LOW → native USB**, **HIGH → CAN**. State survives MCU reset (expander is separately powered) |
| EXIO6 | LCD_VDD_EN | Panel power enable (drive high) |

EXIO0/EXIO7 and OC0–OC3 appear unused.

### 4. Audio — none

Schematic chip list: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, CH422G, CH343P, TJA1051 (CAN), SP3485 (RS485), 2× FSUSB42UMX (USB muxes), CS8501 (battery), SGM2212 (LDO), AP3032/AP3012 (backlight/panel power), NDC7002N (I2C level shift). **No audio codec, no I2S amplifier, no speaker/mic header.** (Source: [schematic PDF](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7-Sch.pdf), wiki feature list.)

### 5. IMU / accelerometer — none

No IMU on board and nothing wired to I2C besides GT911 + CH422G. (Source: schematic, wiki I2C address table.)

### 6. Flash / PSRAM / USB

- **ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8: 16 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM.** PSRAM is **octal/OPI at 120 MHz**; flash QIO 120 MHz (wiki ESP-IDF config block: `CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT=y`, `SPIRAM_SPEED_120M`, `ESPTOOLPY_FLASHMODE_QIO=y`, `FLASHFREQ_120M`). In Arduino IDE: *PSRAM: "OPI PSRAM"*, *Flash Mode: "QIO 120MHz"*. Caveat: wiki's Specifications table says "8 MB Flash" and the schematic U8 label prints "N8R8" — older/inconsistent docs; Features/Onboard-resources/product page all say 16 MB N16R8.
- **Two USB-C ports:**
  - **"USB" port** = ESP32-S3 native USB-OTG on **GPIO19 (D-) / GPIO20 (D+)**, through the FSUSB42UMX mux (EXIO5 LOW). Used by demos for flashing; enter boot mode (hold BOOT) if the port isn't recognized.
  - **"UART" port** = **CH343P** USB-UART bridge (VIO=3.3 V) with auto-download circuit (DTR/RTS → BOOT/EN transistors) onto UART0: **TX=GPIO43, RX=GPIO44**. A slide switch (SW1, "UART selection") routes UART0 either to the CH343P or to the external UART PH2.0 terminal. (Source: schematic U1/U13 + variant header `TX=43, RX=44` + wiki onboard resources.)

### 7. Battery / power

- **PH2.0 3.7 V single-cell Li-ion connector**, charge + 5 V boost via **CS8501**. Default charge current **580 mA** (set by PROG resistor; schematic table: 1.2 kΩ→580 mA, 0.75 kΩ→900 mA, 0.68 kΩ→1000 mA, 5 kΩ→160 mA — wiki says change R45 to adjust). CHG + DONE LEDs, PWR LED. Recommended ≤2000 mAh cell. (Source: schematic U4/J3 + wiki.)
- System rails: 5 V (USB or battery boost) → SGM2212 3.3 V LDO. I2C header has an NDC7002N level translator with a 3 V/5 V selector (H2).

### 8. Other peripherals / GPIO availability

- **TF (microSD) slot:** SPI — MOSI=**11**, SCK=**12**, MISO=**13**, CS=CH422G **EXIO4** (held low; bus exclusive to the card).
- **RS485:** SP3485 (5 V, auto-direction — no DE pin, "RTCN/RTCP" nets are the auto-direction circuit). **ESP32 TX = GPIO16, RX = GPIO15** per Waveshare's own `02_RS485_Test` demo and LCD Wizard — note the wiki table and the arduino-esp32 variant header print them swapped (RXD=16/TXD=15); pins are 15/16 either way. 120 Ω termination jumper J4 (fitted by default).
- **CAN (TWAI):** TJA1051T/3 (VIO=3.3 V), **TX=GPIO20, RX=GPIO19**, shares those pins with native USB via FSUSB42UMX (EXIO5 HIGH = CAN, takes the native USB port away until EXIO5 returns low — survives reset). 120 Ω termination jumper J5. Demos: 50 kbit/s example config.
- **I2C header (PH2.0):** SDA=8/SCL=9, 3.3 V or 5 V selectable (level shifter). Avoid slave addresses 0x20–0x27, 0x30–0x3F (CH422G), 0x5D (GT911).
- **"Sensor AD" terminal:** **GPIO6** analog input (demo: 12-bit ADC, `analogReadMilliVolts`; header 3V3/AD/GND with divider/protection network).
- **No RTC chip, no audio, no IMU** on board.
- **Free GPIOs: effectively none.** The RGB panel eats 20 pins; touch/I2C 8/9, IRQ 4, SD 11–13, RS485 15/16, USB/CAN 19/20, UART0 43/44, ADC 6 (on the sensor header). GPIO0/45/46 are strapping pins *and* LCD data/sync lines (works because the panel holds them via 10 k pulls at boot, per schematic). External expansion = I2C header + GPIO6 ADC + optional UART header + CAN/RS485 terminals. BOOT and RESET buttons onboard.

## Sources

- Kept: [Waveshare wiki — ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7) — pinout tables, CH422G mapping, IDF memory config, I2C address map, battery notes
- Kept: [Schematic PDF (V1.2)](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7-Sch.pdf) — definitive chip list (CH343P, TJA1051, SP3485, FSUSB42UMX ×2, CS8501, AP3032/AP3012), EXIO6=LCD_VDD_EN, muxes, battery resistor table; confirms absence of audio/IMU/RTC
- Kept: [waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 GitHub repo](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7) — 08_DrawColorBar (`waveshare_lcd_port.h`: 16 MHz, 4/8/8/4/8/8 timing, data pin order), 03_SD_Test (CH422G EXIO1–5 demo use), 02_RS485_Test (TX16/RX15), 04_Sensor_AD (GPIO6), bundled `BOARD_WAVESHARE_ESP32_S3_TOUCH_LCD_7.h` (GT911 0x5D/400 kHz, PCLK_ACTIVE_NEG=1, backlight SWITCH_EXPANDER EXIO2, expander nominal 0x20)
- Kept: [arduino-esp32 variant pins_arduino.h (3.3.10)](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/3.3.10/variants/waveshare_esp32_s3_touch_lcd_7/pins_arduino.h) — board is a first-class Arduino core target ("Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7", USB PID 0x8234), confirms all LCD/touch/CH422G pins, UART0 43/44
- Kept: [LCD Wizard — waveshare-s3-7](https://lcdwizard.com/boards/waveshare-s3-7) — independent community verification incl. Arduino_GFX (GFX Library for Arduino) pin order, EXIO6 panel-enable requirement, USB/CAN mux reset persistence, RS485 direction note
- Kept: [Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel.cpp (Arduino_GFX master)](https://github.com/moononournation/Arduino_GFX/blob/master/src/databus/Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel.cpp) — polarity semantics (`polarity==1` → idle high), fb_in_psram hardcoded, data-pin ordering (B first, then G, R — matches D0..D15 table above), default speed 12 MHz on OPI
- Kept: [ESP32_IO_Expander — esp_io_expander_ch422g.h](https://github.com/esp-arduino-libs/ESP32_IO_Expander/blob/master/src/port/esp_io_expander_ch422g.h) — `ESP_IO_EXPANDER_I2C_CH422G_ADDRESS=0x24` (ignored by chip protocol)
- Kept: [Waveshare docs — Section 07 Driving RGB565 Screen](https://docs.waveshare.com/docs/ESP32/ESP32-S3/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/Arduino/Arduino-RGB-LCD-Demo) — ST7262 nature, EXIO2 DISP note, code walkthrough
- Dropped: Home Assistant community thread on brightness — anecdotal, suggests GPIO6 PWM rewiring; not authoritative
- Dropped: NuttX board docs — restate wiki table, nothing extra

## Gaps

- **RS485 TX/RX labeling conflicts** between Waveshare's demo (TX=16/RX=15, matches SP3485 DI/RO wiring) and the wiki table / arduino-esp32 variant (TX=15/RX=16). Pins are 15/16 regardless — swap in software if the link is dead.
- **pclk_active_neg** differs between Waveshare's own paths (board config=1, positional-ctor demo=0); both reportedly work. Recommend 1.
- The exact analog **input voltage range** of the Sensor AD divider (LCD Wizard says 0–3.1 V; the 200 kΩ/100 kΩ network suggests a ÷3 divider → ~0–9 V external). Confirm on hardware before scaling.
- Schematic text shows module marked "N8R8" and the wiki spec table "8 MB Flash"; all other sources say N16R8/16 MB. Verify with `esptool.py flash_id` on the actual unit.
- ESP-IDF demo package (separate from the Arduino repo) was not fetched; its LVGL benchmark note (21 MHz) is from the wiki. Not needed for an Arduino_GFX port.

## Port checklist (agent-buddy firmware)

1. Board target: arduino-esp32 ≥3.0.6 has "Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7"; else ESP32-S3 Dev Module with PSRAM=OPI, Flash=QIO 120 MHz, USB CDC if logging via native USB.
2. Init I2C (SDA=8, SCL=9, 400 k) → CH422G: all outputs; EXIO6=1 (panel VDD), EXIO3 pulse (LCD reset), EXIO2=1 (backlight), EXIO5=0 (keep native USB for the app/daemon link), EXIO4 low only if SD used.
3. `Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel` + `Arduino_RGB_Display` as in the snippet above; framebuffer 800×480×2 = 768 KB from octal PSRAM.
4. Touch: GT911 @0x5D on the same Wire, INT=4 (input), RST=EXIO1 with the GT911 INT-low address-select sequence.
5. Backlight is on/off only — brightness control would need AP3032 FB-circuit mod; do not promise PWM dimming.

# Progress: ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 pin-level research

Status: complete.

Fetched and cross-checked: Waveshare wiki, schematic PDF (V1.2), waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 demo repo (cloned locally, read 05+ demo/lib files incl. bundled BOARD_WAVESHARE_ESP32_S3_TOUCH_LCD_7.h and BusRGB source), arduino-esp32 3.3.10 variant pins_arduino.h, ESP32_IO_Expander CH422G header, LCD Wizard board preset, Arduino_GFX Arduino_ESP32RGBPanel source (polarity semantics).

All 8 task questions answered with concrete GPIOs. Final brief written to /tmp/lcd7-research.md.

Notable findings beyond the obvious:
- Backlight is CH422G EXIO2 on/off only (AP3032 boost); panel power gate is EXIO6 (LCD_VDD_EN) — must drive BOTH for a visible image.

## Findings
1. **RGB panel pins** — DE=5, VSYNC=3, HSYNC=46, PCLK=7. Data (R0..R4 / G0..G5 / B0..B4 in Arduino_GFX arg order): R=1,2,42,41,40; G=39,0,45,48,47,21; B=14,38,18,17,10 (panel bits R3–R7/G2–G7/B3–B7; esp_lcd D0–D15 = 14,38,18,17,10,39,0,45,48,47,21,1,2,42,41,40). Identical across wiki, demo `waveshare_lcd_port.h`, the ESP32_Display_Panel board config, and the arduino-esp32 3.3.10 variant header. [Wiki](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7) · [variant pins_arduino.h](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/blob/3.3.10/variants/waveshare_esp32_s3_touch_lcd_7/pins_arduino.h) · [demo repo](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7)
2. **Timing/polarity** — PCLK 16 MHz; HPW/HBP/HFP=4/8/8, VPW/VBP/VFP=4/8/8; bounce buffer 8000 px; sync idle **high** (esp_lcd defaults, i.e. Arduino_GFX `hsync_polarity=1, vsync_polarity=1`); `pclk_active_neg=1` in the LVGL board config (the color-bar demo's positional ctor leaves it 0 — both work on ST7262); IDF benchmark at 21 MHz ≈ 51 Hz refresh.
3. **Backlight** — **not a GPIO, not PWM**: CH422G **EXIO2** (`DISP`), on/off active-high, via AP3032 boost driver. Panel power (AVDD/VGH/VGL) separately gated by CH422G **EXIO6** (`LCD_VDD_EN`) — drive both high. [Schematic](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7-Sch.pdf) · [board config](https://github.com/waveshareteam/ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7)
4. **Touch** — GT911 @ **0x5D** (INT-low-at-reset selects it), I2C SDA=8/SCL=9 @400 kHz, **INT=GPIO4**, **RST=CH422G EXIO1**. Reset sequence: INT out-low → EXIO1 low 100 ms → high → 200 ms → INT input.

EXIO1=TP_RST, EXIO2=backlight, EXIO3=LCD_RST, EXIO4=SD_CS (held low), EXIO5=USB_SEL/CAN_SEL (**LOW=native USB, HIGH=CAN**; survives MCU reset), EXIO6=LCD_VDD_EN. Nominal address 0x24 (ESP32_IO_Expander, ignored by chip protocol; board conf uses 0x20). [CH422G header](https://github.com/esp-arduino-libs/ESP32_IO_Expander)
6. **Audio/IMU/RTC** — **none on board** (schematic chip list: CH343P, CH422G, TJA1051, SP3485, 2× FSUSB42UMX, CS8501, SGM2212, AP3032/AP3012, NDC7002N level shifter).
7. **USB** — two Type-C ports: native USB-OTG on **GPIO19(D-)/20(D+)** (through EXIO5 mux; shared with CAN TX=20/RX=19 via TJA1051) and a **CH343P** USB-UART bridge to UART0 **TX=43/RX=44** with auto-download circuit; slide switch routes UART0 to either CH343P or the external UART header.
8. **Battery/power** — PH2.0 3.7 V cell, CS8501 charge+5 V boost, 580 mA default charge (PROG resistor table: 1.2 k/580 mA, 0.75 k/900 mA, 0.68 k/1000 mA, 5 k/160 mA), CHG/DONE/PWR LEDs.
9. **Other** — TF slot SPI MOSI=11/SCK=12/MISO=13, CS=EXIO4 (permanently selected); RS485 SP3485 auto-direction, demo uses **TX=16/RX=15** (wiki table/variant header print them swapped — pins 15/16 either way); Sensor AD terminal = **GPIO6**; external I2C header (3.3 V/5 V level-shifted); CAN/RS485 120 Ω termination jumpers fitted. **Essentially no free GPIO** beyond GPIO6 + the I2C/UART/CAN/RS485 headers; GPIO0/45/46 double as LCD lines (OK at boot).

- Dropped: Home Assistant forum thread (anecdotal backlight-PWM rewiring), NuttX docs (restates wiki).
